of the dispute.
Step Three—Referral to Industrial Relations
(8) If the dispute is not able to be resolved within the business area by step one or step two, it
will be referred to the Industrial Relations team and may be referred to the National
Manager in charge of human resources for resolution.
Referral to the Fair Work Commission
(9) If a dispute is unable to be resolved at the workplace level, and all appropriate steps under
sub-sections 99(5) - (8) above have been taken, a party to the dispute may refer the
dispute to the Fair Work Commission.
(10) The Fair Work Commission may deal with the dispute in two stages:
(a) the Fair Work Commission will first attempt to resolve the dispute as it considers
appropriate, including by mediation, conciliation, expressing an opinion or making a
recommendation; and
(b) if the Fair Work Commission is unable to resolve the dispute at the first stage, the
Fair Work Commission may then:
(i) arbitrate the dispute; and
(ii) make a determination that is binding on the parties.
Note: If the Fair Work Commission arbitrates the dispute, it may also use the powers that
are available to it under the Fair Work Act. A decision that the Fair Work Commission makes
when arbitrating a dispute is a decision for the purpose of Div 3 of Part 5.1 of the Fair Work
Act. Therefore, an appeal may be made against the decision.
(11) While the parties are attempting to resolve the dispute using the procedures in this term:
(a) an Employee must continue to perform their work as they would normally in
accordance with established custom and practice at the AFP that existed
immediately prior to the dispute arising unless they have a reasonable concern
about an imminent risk to their health or safety; and
(b) subject to sub-section 99(11)(a) above, an Employee must comply with a direction
given by the AFP to perform other available work at the same workplace, or at
another workplace, unless:
(i) the work is not safe; or
(ii) applicable work health and safety legislation would not permit the work to be
performed; or
(iii) the work is not appropriate for the Employee to perform; or
(iv) there are other reasonable grounds for the Employee to refuse to comply with
the direction.
(12) The parties to the dispute agree to be bound by a decision made by the Fair Work

100.Delegates' Rights
(1) Union delegates play an important and legitimate role in the workplace. This includes
representing their members and supporting Employee access to union officials, and
providing Employee views to the AFP.
(2) The role of union delegates is to be respected and supported.
(3) The AFP and union delegates will work together respectfully and collaboratively.
Supporting the role of union delegates
(4) The AFP respects the role of union delegates to:
(a) provide information, consult with and seek feedback from Employees in the
workplace on workplace matters;
(b) consult with other delegates and union officials, and get advice and assistance from
union officials;
(c) represent the interests of members to the AFP and industrial tribunals; and
(d) represent members at relevant union forums, consultative committees or
bargaining.
(5) The AFP and union delegates recognise that undertaking the role of a union delegate is
not the primary purpose of an Employee’s engagement, and must work with and not
unreasonably impact their regular duties. Honorary officials may request additional time
and facilities from time to time.
(6) Union delegates will be provided with reasonable paid time during their Normal Working
Hours to perform their union delegate role. The paid time provided should not result in
disruption to critical services or Operational Requirements.
(7) To support the role of union delegates, the AFP will, subject to legislative and Operational
Requirements, including privacy and security requirements:

(2) Movement through the band levels and Increment Points of the Team Member/Constable

So you want to join the AFP? Follow these tips to give yourself the best chance of success.

On this page
Your pitch
Preparing for interview
Selecting referees
Create your pitch
A pitch is a summary of your claims for the position you're applying for. Be concise, consistent and clear.

Before you start your pitch, make sure you read and understand:

the position requirements and responsibilities
the selection criteria
the position's work level standard
other relevant information, such as team overview and key working relationships.
In your pitch:

address the selection criteria and role requirements
outline why you're suitable and what you can bring to the role.
Get in touch with the contact person for the position if you need more details.

What to include in your pitch
Your pitch is not your career history and experience. That belongs in your résumé.

Your pitch needs to show:

your attributes as they relate to the work level standards
your potential to perform the role, including any leadership qualities.
Use examples to highlight your career successes, and address:

what challenges you faced
how you overcame the challenges
the outcome of the challenge.
Close with a strong statement about why we should choose you for the role.

Pitch dos and don'ts
Do:

Address the selection criteria and role requirements.
Identify your key messages and stay focused.
Use one or 2 work-relevant examples that address all criteria rather than separate examples for each.
Link examples back to your résumé.
Check your response for relevance, typos and flow before submitting.
Don't:

Use dot points.
Waste space simply telling us about projects or experience already in your résumé.
Use small font or narrow margins to maximise word usage, making it too hard for us to read.
Submit a pitch longer than 2 pages, which shows you haven't crafted a succinct and highly relevant response.
Make your pitch and resume work together
Your résumé and your pitch should align. When read together, they must clearly address the position's selection criteria.

Résumés usually include your:

contact details
relevant education, qualifications and technical skills
work experience, including responsibilities and achievements
details of referees.
In your pitch, encourage us to refer to your résumé for details.

Prepare for your interview
Before your interview, prepare by:

reviewing your responses to the selection criteria
picking a few extra examples to use in the interview
participating in a mock interview using the selection criteria and job description to think of possible questions
looking at our website to understand what we do – our annual report and corporate plan may be helpful.
During the interview:

take time to think about your answer
try to respond to interview questions using the STAR method
ask the selection panel to rephrase the question if you don't understand
take a copy of your application or other notes with you for quick reference.
The STAR method
The STAR method is a way of presenting information against selection criteria. For each criterion, think about the following and use these points to form sentences:

Situation: set the context by describing a situation where you used the skills or qualities and gained the experience.
Task: outline your role.
Actions: explain what you did and how you did it.
Results: describe what you achieved and how it relates to our vacant position.
Choose your referees
We'll often ask you for the names and contact details of 2 referees.

Your referees should:

be current or former supervisors or someone who can establish your suitability for the vacant position
have observed you in the workplace (ideally)
have witnessed how you respond in a range of relevant situations
be able to confidently and honestly respond to questioning or be prepared to provide comments in writing about your suitability for the vacant position
understand that any comments they give may be given to you as part of feedback processes or other mechanisms
not be a spouse, partner, immediate family member or close associate.
When you choose your referees, make sure you ask them if they're okay for us to contact them about your suitability for the position. Don't assume that just because an individual is your manager, they will or should be your referee. And make sure they will be available by phone or email.

If you can, give your referees copies of the job description, your résumé and your pitch. Talk to them about why you are suitable for the role.

Over the longer term, take a strategic approach to referees. Develop relationships with a wide range of people who can confidently speak on your behalf, such as senior managers, clients, key stakeholders or community leaders.

Keep in touch with your referees. They may move to different roles, which could affect whether you can still call on them.

Referee checks
We'll check with your referees to confirm the information you provide in:

your application and résumé
your interview
any related assessments.
The checks may relate to your work performance, attitude, experience, qualifications, skillset and other work-related qualities.

Australians hold us to the highest level of integrity, both on and off duty. Integrity is critical to our success and to maintaining the trust of the Australian Government, other stakeholders and the community.

Our people have access to sensitive and classified information, areas and equipment. We're trusted with intrusive powers to fulfil our responsibilities.

That's why, to work with us, you must meet AFP's character standards. When you're shortlisted as a potential candidate, you'll need to fill out our Employment Suitability Questionnaire (ESQ). This helps us assess your character and your ability to comply with our professional standards in your official duties and personal life.

You'll need to give us as much detail as possible about:

all convictions or cautions, including from when you were younger than 18
illicit drug use
firearms use, including reasons for any firearm licence refusal or unlawful history of firearms
people you know who could be a ‘declarable association’.
A declarable association is a private relationship with an individual, group, event or organisation that could impact your reputation or integrity – and ours.

If you can't meet our character standards, your application will not progress. We also apply an exclusion period, which means you can't re-apply to join the AFP for a certain length of time.

The AFP Manager or Commander Professional Standards is the delegate who assesses each questionnaire.

You'll be assessed against AFP's core values:

integrity
commitment
excellence
accountability
fairness
trust
respect.
The delegate's decision is final, so we won't review their decision if you don't pass.

Criminal history
As part of the ESQ, you must declare your full criminal history, including juvenile records and spent convictions.

Juvenile records
Disclose all cautions and convictions you received when younger than 18. Give as much detail as possible, for example:

guilty
not guilty
caution
restorative justice
diversionary conferencing.
Spent convictions
Disclose all previous charges and convictions, including spent convictions.

Spent convictions are not disclosed on a National Police Certificate. But when applying for a job with us, you must disclose them. We need to see your complete criminal record.

When employing staff, AFP and other law enforcement agencies are exempt from the 'non-disclosure' provisions in the Commonwealth Spent Convictions Scheme under Part VIIC, Division 3 of the Crimes Act 1914 (Cth).

Traffic history
Provide the details of all driving licences you've held, including learner's permits (Ls) and provisional licences (Ps).

You must provide your traffic history that:

covers all states, territories and countries where you have held a licence for the past 10 years.
is no older than 3 months from when we first asked you for it
continuously covers the last 10 years you have held a licence.
If you have held a driving licence for less than 10 years, provide traffic history for the period held.

Include the full document you get from each licencing authority. The documents do not need to be certified.

We will not accept:

an issued traffic infringement notice
demerit points record
a copy of your driver's licence
a National Police Certificate check
any documents obtained through Freedom of Information (FOI) laws.
If you've held a licence or driven overseas, and can't provide a copy of your overseas driving history, submit a statutory declaration stating:

the period you held your licence
any traffic offences you are aware of.
If you've never held a driver's licence, or never driven and received an infringement of any kind, let us know. You'll need to submit a statutory declaration for this.

Alcohol and drug use
Drugs, alcohol and pharmaceutical abuse have serious effects on society. We expect the highest standards of integrity and professionalism from our people.
Under the Australian Federal Police Regulations 2018 (Cth), we can test AFP appointees for: 

alcohol
pharmaceutical drug abuse
prohibited (illicit) drugs.
Our staff must comply with any written direction to provide a body sample for drug or alcohol testing. It's a serious breach of AFP's professional standards if they disobey a direction or fail to undergo drug or alcohol testing.

Prohibited (illicit) drugs
Declare all illicit drug use, including what, when and how. If you're unsure of the exact dates of your last illicit drug use, provide as much detail as possible. At a minimum, include the year of your drug use and how many times.

Previous drug use won't immediately result in an unsuccessful application.

We have a zero-tolerance drug policy. Once you have submitted your application, you must stop all illicit drug use, and this includes using:

prohibited drugs here and overseas, regardless of whether the drug has been decriminalised or legalised
selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs) except within lawful controlled medical parameters set by a registered medical authority
cannabinoids, unless prescribed by an authorised Australian registered health practitioner.
Pharmaceutical drug abuse
Pharmaceutical drug abuse includes taking:

prescription medication not prescribed to you
prescription medication outside the prescribed parameters, such as exceeding the prescribed dosage
taking over-the-counter pharmaceutical products outside normal medical parameters, such as exceeding the recommended dosage or taking them for an unintended purpose.
Alcohol
When an AFP employee is on duty, or returning to duty, their blood alcohol concentration must not exceed 0.02 g of alcohol in 210 L of breath or 100 ml of blood.

Declarable associations
Declare any person, group, event or organisation you know that could be a declarable association, such as:

known criminals
any person, including a family member, suspected to be engaged in criminal activity, including ‘social’ drug use
criminal entities
any person, including a family member, closely affiliated with or related to known criminals
any person, including a family member, group or organisation, known or perceived to be involved in unlawful activity
any person, including a family member, involved in a group or organisation known or perceived to be involved in unlawful activity
personal contact or relationships with journalists or media representatives.
Give as much detail as possible, including:

full name and date of birth of each declared associate
reasons why you believe there may be a conflict of interest
how often you interact with them.
Declaring criminal or inappropriate associations does not automatically prevent an application from proceeding. However, failing to disclose any required information may result in your application being unsuccessful.

Exclusion periods
We assess applications holistically and on a case‐by‐case basis.

Depending on the information provided, AFP's delegate may use their discretion to apply an exclusion period if you disclose a conviction or integrity issue.

An exclusion period means you can't re-apply to join the AFP for a certain length of time.

The exclusion period will:

depend on the nature of the issue
start from the date of your conviction or integrity issue.
AFP's recommended exclusion periods for prior convictions or integrity issues
Conviction or integrity issue	Recommended period of exclusion
Terminated or dismissed from any employment	Delegate discretion
Inappropriate and/or Criminal associations	Delegate discretion
Any sentence of imprisonment, including suspended sentences and periodic detention	Delegate discretion
Subject of a current or outstanding arrest warrant, including first instance and family law	Delegate discretion
Declarations that indicate past behaviour is inconsistent with the professional standards of the AFP and not in alignment with AFP values. These include but are not limited to the following.

racism
misogyny
adverse media attention that may cause reputational damage to the AFP
Delegate discretion
An indictable offence, including indictable offence heard summarily	5 year
Offence for assault, hinder, obstruct or resist a Police Officer or any other public official	5 year
Personal violence offences, including assault occasioning bodily harm	5 to 10 years
Domestic or family violences offences or behaviour	10 years
Sexual harassment offences or behaviour	10 years
Sexual assault or abuse offences or behaviour	15 years to indefinite
Dishonesty offences, including fraud, obtaining benefit by deception, forgery or impersonation	5 to 10 years
Corruption activities or related offences	Delegate discretion
Firearm or weapon-related offences	5 years
Summary offence not outlined in this section on more than one occasion	Delegate discretion
Offence for driving under the influence of illicit drugs	Delegate discretion
The applicant knowingly or deliberately fails to disclose relevant information or provides false or misleading information during the application process	5 years
Illicit drug related offences, including the manufacture, sale or distribution, on any occasion in any country, of substances that are illegal or prohibited in Australia	5 to 10 years
The applicant fails to satisfy the requirements to obtain a security clearance	5 years
Subject (respondent) of a current court ordered apprehended violence order or equivalent; or a current interim apprehended violence order or equivalent	5 years
Subject (respondent) of an apprehended violence order or equivalent which has expired, been dismissed or revoked	2 to 5 years
Subject (respondent) of an order under firearms or weapon legislation that prohibits the person from possession or using a firearm	2 to 5 years
One conviction for a public order or minor street offence	1 year
One conviction for any criminal (wilful) damage to property offence	3 years
One formal Breach of the Peace or Move on Notice	1 to 3 years
One lodgement or charge for intoxication or disorderly behaviour in a public place	Delegate discretion
One conviction for a theft or stealing offence (single offences as a juvenile only)	1 to 5 years
One conviction for a receiving or possessing stolen property offence (single offences as a juvenile only)	1 to 5 years
Exclusion periods also apply for traffic infringements and convictions. Any exclusion period will start from the date of your infringement or conviction.

 

AFP's recommended exclusion periods for traffic offences
Conviction or infringement within the last 10 years	Recommended period of exclusion
One conviction for low-range driving under the influence (0.05 g or more but less than 0.08 g)	1 year
One conviction for mid‐range driving under the influence (0.08 g or more but less than 0.15 g)	3 years
One conviction for a high-range driving under the influence (0.15 g or more)	5 years
Three or more convictions for driving under the influence (any range)	15 years
Licence suspension due to accumulated demerit points	2 years
Licence suspension for any other reason	Delegate discretion
Other minor driving or traffic offences, including:

low to mid‐range speed (less than 25 km/h over the speed limit)
using a mobile phone
not wearing a seatbelt
1 year from most recent offence, if an applicant has 5 or more minor traffic offences across the past 3 years

2 years from the date of most recent offence, if an applicant has 4 or more minor traffic offences in the past 12 months

Consideration for exclusion if total of minor offences is excessive (i.e. exceeds total years of driving)

Serious traffic or driving offences such as:

negligent driving
any ‘hoon’ offence resulting in disqualification or suspension of licence
driving while disqualified or suspended
dangerous driving
negligent driving causing injury
high-range speed (more than 25 km/h over the speed limit)
drug-impaired driving
5 years, or discretion depending on circumstances

# M365 Collaboration Specialist - Job Application Pitch

## Introduction

As a seasoned Microsoft 365 specialist with extensive experience in implementing and optimizing collaboration platforms, I am excited to apply for the M365 Collaboration Specialist role with the Australian Federal Police. My technical expertise in SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and the broader M365 ecosystem, combined with my proven track record of delivering enterprise solutions, positions me to make an immediate contribution to the AFP's digital workplace strategy.

## Technical Expertise and Experience

My journey as an M365 specialist spans over 15 years, during which I've mastered SharePoint and Teams administration, information architecture design, and governance implementation. My experience includes:

- **Leading M365 implementations**: Successfully delivered Microsoft 365 migrations and implementations across multiple industries, with documented experience in over 9,000 professional client interactions.

- **SharePoint expertise**: Designed and implemented complex SharePoint site architectures, navigation structures, and metadata frameworks that balance security requirements with user experience.

- **Teams governance**: Developed comprehensive governance models for Teams deployment, focusing on secure collaboration while maintaining regulatory compliance.

- **Security and compliance**: Implemented robust security models and permission structures to protect sensitive information, a critical skill for an organisation like the AFP handling classified information.

- **PowerShell automation**: Created automation scripts to streamline administration tasks, improve consistency, and reduce manual effort.

## Alignment with AFP Requirements

The job advertisement highlights several key requirements that align perfectly with my experience:

### M365 Administration and SharePoint Experience
I significantly exceed the minimum requirement of 3 years of M365 Administration and SharePoint experience, bringing 15+ years of hands-on expertise with SharePoint since 2009 and comprehensive knowledge across all aspects of the M365 platform. My extensive experience spans multiple SharePoint versions from on-premises (2007, 2010, 2013, 2016) to SharePoint Online, including managing complex permission structures, implementing governance frameworks, and guiding organizations through cloud migrations.

### Technical Knowledge
My technical skillset encompasses all the required technologies:
- Microsoft Azure Cloud administration and user migration
- SharePoint Online site architecture and governance
- OneDrive for Business deployment and management
- Teams configuration and adoption strategies
- Hands-on scripting with PowerShell and Azure CLI

### Technical Documentation
Throughout my career, I've created comprehensive technical documentation, including:
- Detailed knowledge base articles for service desk reference
- End-user training materials and adoption guides
- Process documentation and standard operating procedures
- Governance frameworks and security models

### Stakeholder Engagement
My experience includes:
- Leading client consultations and requirements gathering sessions
- Conducting user training and adoption workshops
- Collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver integrated solutions
- Regular communication with leadership on project status and strategic initiatives

## Driving Collaboration and Innovation

In addition to meeting the technical requirements, I bring a strategic mindset focused on driving adoption and maximizing the value of M365 investments:

1. **User-centric approach**: I prioritise understanding user needs to create intuitive, efficient collaboration solutions that enhance productivity while maintaining security.

2. **Innovation leadership**: I continuously explore new M365 capabilities and identify opportunities to advance existing implementations, ensuring organisations get maximum value from their Microsoft investment.

3. **Knowledge sharing**: I'm passionate about empowering users and IT teams through comprehensive training and knowledge transfer, creating a culture of continuous learning.

4. **Process optimisation**: I excel at identifying manual processes that can be automated and streamlined using M365 tools, increasing organisational efficiency.

## Client Portfolio Highlights

My experience spans diverse organizations and industries, providing me with a broad perspective on collaboration needs:

- **Large enterprises**: Implemented enterprise-wide collaboration solutions for organizations with 10,000+ users, demonstrating ability to handle complex environments like the AFP.

- **Government agencies**: Worked with multiple government entities, including local councils and statutory authorities, giving me insight into public sector requirements and security considerations.

- **Technology companies**: Partnered with technology firms to optimize their collaboration platforms, developing advanced solutions that leverage the full capabilities of M365.

This diverse client base has equipped me with the versatility to understand different organisational needs and communication styles, an asset when working across the various commands within the AFP.

## Commitment to AFP's Mission

I am drawn to the AFP's mission of providing dynamic and effective law enforcement to the Australian people. The opportunity to support this vital work by enhancing collaboration capabilities is particularly meaningful to me. I understand that effective collaboration tools are critical for information sharing in law enforcement, and I am committed to ensuring AFP personnel have secure, reliable, and efficient platforms to support their important work.

## Conclusion

The M365 Collaboration Specialist role at the AFP represents an ideal opportunity to apply my technical expertise and strategic approach to collaboration in support of a mission-critical organisation. I am confident that my experience in implementing, optimising, and governing Microsoft 365 platforms will enable me to make significant contributions to the AFP's digital workplace strategy, enhancing collaboration while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance.

I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience align with the AFP's needs and to demonstrate my passion for creating effective collaboration solutions.

- Led MS Purview design and implementation for multiple Federal/State Government agencies, ensuring compliance with Australian Government security requirements
- Developed SharePoint Online intranet solutions for organizations with 30,000+ users, improving information access and collaboration# CAMERON STEWART
## M365 Collaboration Specialist | SharePoint Administrator | Teams Expert

**Location:** Perth, WA  
**Email:** info@cameronstewart.com.au  
**Phone:** 0405 335 677  
**Citizenship:** Australian Citizen  
**Security Clearance:** Negative Vetting 1 (NV1)

---

## PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

Information Management & Collaboration Specialist with 20+ years of experience in Microsoft 365 ecosystem design, implementation, and governance. Successfully delivered enterprise M365 projects for 40+ clients, including SharePoint Online intranets for 30,000+ users and MS Purview implementations for Federal/State Government agencies. Strong expertise in developing and documenting technical processes for service desk teams and implementing governance frameworks that balance security with usability.

---

## PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

### Principal Analyst
**The Waffle Co | July 2018 – Present**

*Leading the implementation, optimization, and governance of Microsoft 365 collaboration tools for government and enterprise clients.*

**Key Responsibilities:**
- Implement, maintain, and administer Microsoft 365 collaborative tooling platforms, focusing on Teams and SharePoint
- Develop, test, and implement policies and procedures to mature M365 ecosystem
- Document processes, procedures, and techniques for operational handover
- Create comprehensive, product-ready documentation for user and technical audiences
- Interface with service desk teams to ensure proper knowledge transfer
- Develop and maintain clear technical guides and configuration documentation

docs.content:
# M365 Collaboration Specialist - Job Application Pitch

## Introduction

As a seasoned Microsoft 365 specialist with extensive experience in implementing and optimising collaboration platforms, I am excited to apply for the M365 Collaboration Specialist role with the Australian Federal Police. My technical expertise in SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and the broader M365 ecosystem, combined with my proven track record of delivering enterprise solutions, positions me to make an immediate contribution to the AFP's digital workplace strategy.

## Technical Expertise and Experience

My journey as an M365 specialist spans over 15 years, during which I've mastered SharePoint and Teams administration, information architecture design, and governance implementation. My experience includes:

- **Leading M365 implementations**: Successfully delivered Microsoft 365 migrations and implementations across multiple industries, with documented experience in over 9,000 professional client interactions.

- **SharePoint expertise**: Designed and implemented complex SharePoint site architectures, navigation structures, and metadata frameworks that balance security requirements with user experience.

- **Teams governance**: Developed comprehensive governance models for Teams deployment, focusing on secure collaboration while maintaining regulatory compliance.

- **Security and compliance**: Implemented robust security models and permission structures to protect sensitive information, a critical skill for an organisation like the AFP handling classified information.

- **PowerShell automation**: Created automation scripts to streamline administration tasks, improve consistency, and reduce manual effort.

## Alignment with AFP Requirements

The job advertisement highlights several key requirements that align perfectly with my experience:

### M365 Administration and SharePoint Experience
I significantly exceed the minimum requirement of 3 years of M365 Administration and SharePoint experience, bringing 15+ years of hands-on expertise with SharePoint since 2009 and comprehensive knowledge across all aspects of the M365 platform. My extensive experience spans multiple SharePoint versions from on-premises (2007, 2010, 2013, 2016) to SharePoint Online, including managing complex permission structures, implementing governance frameworks, and guiding organisations through cloud migrations.

### Technical Knowledge
My technical skillset encompasses all the required technologies:
- Microsoft Azure Cloud administration and user migration
- SharePoint Online site architecture and governance
- OneDrive for Business deployment and management
- Teams configuration and adoption strategies
- Hands-on scripting with PowerShell and Azure CLI

### Technical Documentation
Throughout my career, I've created comprehensive technical documentation, including:
- Detailed knowledge base articles for service desk reference
- End-user training materials and adoption guides
- Process documentation and standard operating procedures
- Governance frameworks and security models

### Stakeholder Engagement
My experience includes:
- Leading client consultations and requirements gathering sessions
- Conducting user training and adoption workshops
- Collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver integrated solutions
- Regular communication with leadership on project status and strategic initiatives

## Driving Collaboration and Innovation

In addition to meeting the technical requirements, I bring a strategic mindset focused on driving adoption and maximising the value of M365 investments:

1. **User-centric approach**: I prioritise understanding user needs to create intuitive, efficient collaboration solutions that enhance productivity while maintaining security.

2. **Innovation leadership**: I continuously explore new M365 capabilities and identify opportunities to advance existing implementations, ensuring organisations get maximum value from their Microsoft investment.

3. **Knowledge sharing**: I'm passionate about empowering users and IT teams through comprehensive training and knowledge transfer, creating a culture of continuous learning.

4. **Process optimisation**: I excel at identifying manual processes that can be automated and streamlined using M365 tools, increasing organisational efficiency.

## Client Portfolio Highlights

My experience spans diverse organisations and industries, providing me with a broad perspective on collaboration needs:

- **Large enterprises**: Implemented enterprise-wide collaboration solutions for organisations with 10,000+ users, demonstrating ability to handle complex environments like the AFP.

- **Government agencies**: Worked with multiple government entities, including local councils and statutory authorities, giving me insight into public sector requirements and security considerations.

- **Technology companies**: Partnered with technology firms to optimise their collaboration platforms, developing advanced solutions that leverage the full capabilities of M365.

This diverse client base has equipped me with the versatility to understand different organisational needs and communication styles, an asset when working across the various commands within the AFP.

## Commitment to AFP's Mission

I am drawn to the AFP's mission of providing dynamic and effective law enforcement to the Australian people. The opportunity to support this vital work by enhancing collaboration capabilities is particularly meaningful to me. I understand that effective collaboration tools are critical for information sharing in law enforcement, and I am committed to ensuring AFP personnel have secure, reliable, and efficient platforms to support their important work.

## Conclusion

The M365 Collaboration Specialist role at the AFP represents an ideal opportunity to apply my technical expertise and strategic approach to collaboration in support of a mission-critical organisation. I am confident that my experience in implementing, optimising, and governing Microsoft 365 platforms will enable me to make significant contributions to the AFP's digital workplace strategy, enhancing collaboration while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance.

I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience align with the AFP's needs and to demonstrate my passion for creating effective collaboration solutions.

#  Project Control Group Briefing

**Meeting date:** 22/04/2025

**Subject**: Service Directory

**Appendices:**

Draft Procedure -- Service Directory

Service Directory Requirements for the Developer**\
**

**Author:** Melissa Evans and Brodie Preston

**\
**

1.  **PURPOSE:**

> To provide an update on the work completed to date on the service
> directory and the proposed next steps.

2.  **BACKGROUND:**

> "Service Directory" Definition: An internal list of IPC Health
> services or supports.
>
> An Internal Service Directory has been identified as a priority output
> for the SMT project.
>
> Whilst a service directory exists on iHub, staff feedback has
> indicated that this information is not updated in a timely manner, it
> is difficult to search information, and the information is generally
> not trusted (due to not knowing if it is up to date).
>
> An updated Internal Service Directory will be an enabling resource for
> the following SMT action groups:

-   AG3 Referral Forms -- will provide complete and current list of
    services to identify opportunities for online referrals

-   AG4 1300 Number -- will provide valuable resource for call
    responders to know how to answer queries and direct call

-   AG6 Welcoming Clients -- The database of information created could
    also be used to input into information for clients

-   AG8 Holistic needs identification -- will provide complete and
    current list of services to support service navigation

-   AG9 Collaborative Care -- will enable service providers to access a
    complete and current list of services to enable referral and
    multi-disciplinary collaboration.

Concurrent to this work, the Communications team have commenced
discussions around moving the entire Intranet from iHub into SharePoint.
This work directly relates to the Service Directory, as this would be
housed within the new Intranet on SharePoint.

Whilst, completing this work together could be ideal, it would likely
slow down the timeline for the Service Directory, if all other aspects
of the new intranet are being resolved concurrently. However, Service
Delivery project leads will communicate with Intranet working group to
ensure alignment and that any work is considering the bigger picture of
the Intranet.

Note: The need for an updated Staff Directory has also been identified,
however this will be addressed later.

3.  **Key Information:**

The SMT team have been leading the development of a new Internal Service
Directory, considering both where it will live, as well as what
associated procedures and supports are required to keep it up to date.

Actions completed so far:

Meetings with identified stakeholders (November to April):

-   Jo Szczepanska (Digital Health Lead)

-   Ben Letson (ICT)

-   Annette Raijer (Communications)

-   Jane Garnett (People and Culture)

-   Carolyn Uzelac (Manager Communications and Marketing)

-   Joanna Feely (Communications and Engagement Officer)

-   Kylie Thurlow (Manager Governance)

Service information was collected from five teams, including their
feedback on the type of information being included.

Two focus groups were conducted (March) with staff from various back of
house and front of house teams where they:

-   Identified priority information for the service directory

-   Identified preferred platform for the service directory (SharePoint)

-   Identified barriers and solutions to keeping service directory
    information up to date

-   Drafted a procedure for keeping service information up to date

-   Identified technical features desired for the service directory

The following Service Directory elements have been developed:

-   Draft Microsoft Lists (to use as database for information)

-   Draft SharePoint pages (the location of the Service Directory)

-   Draft Procedure -- Service Directory

-   List of technical requirements for the Service Directory

4.  **Next Steps:**

Given the technical expertise and time required to create the service
directory, it is recommended that the development of the Service
Directory is completed by engaging an IT developer to create the service
directory pages and the background automations.

Proposed Project governance:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Project Team**      
  --------------------- -------------------------------------------------
  Project Owner         PCG

  Project Manager       Brodie Preston and Melissa Evans (SMT Team)

  Technical Contact     TBD -- discussions to be had with Comms and IT
  (IT)                  

  Intranet Contact      TBD -- discussions to be had with Comms and IT
  (Comms)               
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Proposed Timeline:**

April/May

-   Engage Developer

-   Developer Creates Site for Service Directory

-   Developer Creates Microsoft List

-   Develop creates survey for information gathering for the Microsoft
    List

-   Developer creates SharePoint pages and sets up required automations
    (Microsoft List to SharePoint page)

-   Developer establishes automated reminders

-   Developer establishes editing rights in Microsoft Lists to
    designated people

-   Testing of new Lists and SharePoint pages with testing teams
    (already established)

-   Approval of Service Directory Procedure

-   Development of Service Directory training materials

June

-   Collection of service information -- all services

-   Training to managers on Service Directory Procedure

July

-   Service Directory published

-   Training to all staff in use of Service Directory

October

-   Evaluation of new service directory and procedure

5.  **Pricing and Revenue- financial details**

Cost for Developer - See Digital Health Lead report provided to ELT
regarding Digital Budget underspend.

6.  **Resource Requirements**

SMT and project team time\
Staff time for testing / training\
System Owner (time ongoing)

7.  **Training Requirements (if applicable)**

Manager training: Awareness of procedure and training in use of required
platforms for updates.

All staff training: Awareness of procedure, training in use of Service
Directory

8.  **Proposed Terms and Conditions (if applicable)**

NA

9.  **Mitigating Measures/ Risk identification and treatment**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Risk**                  **Mitigation/Treatment**
  ------------------------- ---------------------------------------------
  Ongoing time required for Procedure outlines automations/notifications
  system owner              to ease burden

  Staff don't follow        Training for all staff and managers to
  procedure as required     include information regarding importance, how
                            to use and access. Evaluation during
                            implementation to review suitability of
                            procedure.

  Managers don't provide    Promotion at leadership level (team
  service information       meetings), Escalate to PCG
  during development phase  

  There is not a current    Service Directory Procedure identifies need
  clearly defined owner of  to nominate a Technical Owner
  the Intranet

## Creating a new service listing in the Service Directory

When a new service is started at IPC Health, the manager is responsible
for ensuring the service is listed in the Service Directory.

The manager is to contact the System Owner to request a new service
listing in the Service Directory. The [What role is this? What is
considered when \"approving\" as service listing? What is the criteria
to be met?]{.comment-start id="8" author="Kylie Thurlow"
date="2025-04-14T15:16:00Z"}System Owner[]{.comment-end id="8"} will
provide template to the manager for initial content input. The System
Owner approves the new service listing and provides it to the Technical
Owner, who will set up the initial service listing in Microsoft Lists.

The Technical Owner will ensure a SharePoint page is created from this
list and all automations are initiated.

## Nominating the Responsible Person and Accountable Person

The 'accountable person' for all service pages will be the
Manager/Senior Manager of that service/department. The 'accountable
person' is the default 'responsible person' however they can delegate
the 'responsible person' to someone in their team.

This is to be documented in the Service Information (Microsoft List).

To notify the responsible person, users can click on the 'report

## Updating the Service Directory

Regular updating of the Service Directory is essential to ensure that
the information is:

-   Accurate

-   Timely

-   Can be trusted by all users

If information is not updated in a timely manner this will reduce
confidence of all users in the Service Directory as the source of truth
for service information, which will compromise its value for all
services.

There are two key dates listed in the Service Directory to enable users
to know when information was updated.

*Date last reviewed:* The date the information was last reviewed, the
information may or may not have been updated on this date.

*Date last updated:* The date the information was last updated, i.e. the
information was changed.

This enables regular users of the Service Directory to easily identify
if there were any recent changes to information, and to also be informed
that the information has been actively reviewed (i.e. if there have been
no changes for 9 months, however the information has been reviewed in
the last 3 months).

The Service Directory information should be updated when:

-   staff start or finish in the team

-   there are new or changed programs or groups

-   there has been a change in service information (fees, eligibility
    etc)

-   someone reports that content is incorrect

The Service Directory information should be reviewed when:

-   the information hasn't been updated or reviewed in the last 3
    months.[Who will be monitoring this?]{.comment-start id="14"

The Responsible Person will receive a reminder notification to review

# Service Directory - Design Document

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1. Project Overview
The Service Directory is a centralized repository of information about services provided by IPC Health. It aims to provide staff with accurate, up-to-date information about all services offered by the organization, enabling better referrals, improved knowledge sharing, and more efficient service delivery.

### 1.2. Purpose
This document outlines the design specifications for the Service Directory, including data model, user stories, features, and implementation details. It serves as a blueprint for development and a reference for stakeholders.

### 1.3. Scope
The Service Directory will include both client-facing services (such as Audiology, Living Well Program, etc.) and business support services (such as IT). It will provide a standardized structure for service information while allowing for variations between service types.

## 2. User Stories and Requirements

This section outlines what the Service Directory needs to do, using the MoSCoW prioritization method (Must Have, Should Have, Could Have, Won't Have).

### 2.1. Must Have Requirements

1. **As a staff member**, I want to search for services by various parameters, so that I can find relevant services for clients or internal needs.
   
2. **As a staff member**, I want to see which services are available at specific locations, so that I can refer clients to services in their area.
   
3. **As a staff member**, I want to know expected timeframes for support, so that I can provide accurate information to clients about service availability.
   
4. **As a service leader**, I want to update information about my service easily, so that all staff have access to the most current information.
   
5. **As a staff member**, I want to see what a service can and cannot provide, so that I can make appropriate referrals.
   
6. **As a staff member**, I want to know eligibility criteria for services, so that I can determine if a client is eligible.

### 2.2. Should Have Requirements

7. **As a staff member**, I want to see contact information for services, so that I can direct queries appropriately.
   
8. **As a staff member**, I want to see what types of support are available (in-person, telehealth, etc.), so that I can inform clients of service delivery options.
   
9. **As a service leader**, I want to share information about group programs, so that staff can refer appropriate clients.
   
10. **As a staff member**, I want to filter services by tags (e.g., client groups), so that I can find relevant services based on specific needs.

### 2.3. Could Have Requirements

11. **As a staff member**, I want to access the Service Directory on my mobile device, so that I can find information when away from my desk.

12. **As a service leader**, I want to see usage statistics for my service information, so that I can understand how often it is being accessed.

13. **As a staff member**, I want to provide feedback on service information, so that it can be continually improved.

### 2.4. Won't Have Requirements

14. **Public access to the Service Directory** - The directory is for internal staff use only.

15. **Integration with external referral systems** - This functionality may be considered in future phases.

16. **Automated service matching for clients** - The system will provide information but not make automated service recommendations.

17. **Team and staff profiles** - These will be handled by the separate intranet project. The Service Directory is a standalone application focused only on service information.

18. **Automated data migration** - Data migration from existing sources will not be part of the initial implementation. All service information will be entered manually by Service Owners.
   - Source analysis and mapping of legacy data
   - Extract, transform, load processes
   - Migration validation and quality assurance
   
   *Note: A future phase may address data migration if needed.*

## 3. Data Model

### 3.1. Core Service Entity

The Service Directory will be implemented as a SharePoint list with the following fields, organized by logical groupings:

#### Basic Information
| Display Name | Internal Name | SharePoint Field Type | Description | Required |
|--------------|---------------|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| Title | Title | Single line of text | Name of the service | Yes |
| Service Goals | ServiceGoals | Multiple lines of text | One-sentence overview of purpose (Rich text) | Yes |
| Service Type | ServiceType | Choice | Client-facing or Business Support | Yes |
| Service Tags | ServiceTags | Managed Metadata | Taxonomy terms for categorization | No |
| Website URL | WebsiteURL | Hyperlink or Picture | Link to public website for the service | No |

#### Access Information
| Display Name | Internal Name | SharePoint Field Type | Description | Required |
|--------------|---------------|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| Referral Process | ReferralProcess | Multiple lines of text | How to refer clients to the service (Rich text) | Yes |
| Eligibility Criteria | EligibilityCriteria | Multiple lines of text | Who is eligible for the service (Rich text) | Yes |
| Service Contacts | ServiceContacts | Multiple lines of text | Contact information for the service (Rich text) | Yes |
| Service Locations | ServiceLocations | Managed Metadata | Physical locations where service is offered | Yes |
| Wait Times | WaitTimes | Multiple lines of text | Current waiting list information (Rich text) | No |
| Support Timeframes | SupportTimeframes | Multiple lines of text | Expected timeframes for BOH (Rich text) | No |
| Support Request Process | SupportRequestProcess | Multiple lines of text | How to request support for BOH (Rich text) | No |

#### Service Details
| Display Name | Internal Name | SharePoint Field Type | Description | Required |
|--------------|---------------|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| Service Offerings | ServiceOfferings | Multiple lines of text | What the service can help with (Rich text) | Yes |
| Service Exclusions | ServiceExclusions | Multiple lines of text | What the service doesn't provide (Rich text) | No |
| Support Types | SupportTypes | Choice (Multi-select) | In-person, telehealth, etc. | Yes |
| Service Delivery Details | ServiceDeliveryDetails | Multiple lines of text | What clients can expect (Rich text) | No |
| Fees and Costs | FeesAndCosts | Multiple lines of text | Fee structure information (Rich text) | No |

#### Additional Resources
| Display Name | Internal Name | SharePoint Field Type | Description | Required |
|--------------|---------------|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| FAQ | FAQ | Multiple lines of text | Frequently asked questions (Rich text) | No |
| Group Programs | GroupPrograms | Multiple lines of text | Available group programs (Rich text) | No |
| External Services | ExternalServices | Multiple lines of text | Related external services (Rich text) | No |
| Resources | Resources | Multiple lines of text | Links to resources (Rich text) | No |

#### Administration
| Display Name | Internal Name | SharePoint Field Type | Description | Required |
|--------------|---------------|------------------------|-------------|----------|
| Funding Source | FundingSource | Multiple lines of text | How the service is funded (Rich text) | No |
| Service Owner | ServiceOwner | Person or Group | Person responsible for the service and its content | Yes |
| Accountable Person | AccountablePerson | Person or Group | Person accountable for service delivery | Yes |
| Status | Status | Choice | Draft, Published, Archived | Yes |
| Last Review Date | LastReviewDate | Date and Time | Date when service information was last reviewed | Yes |
| Next Review Date | NextReviewDate | Date and Time | Scheduled date for next review | Yes |
| Modified | Modified | Date and Time (System) | Last modified timestamp | Auto |
| Modified By | Editor | Person or Group (System) | Person who last modified | Auto |
| Created | Created | Date and Time (System) | Creation timestamp | Auto |
| Created By | Author | Person or Group (System) | Person who created | Auto |

*Note: The system will use the built-in Modified and Modified By fields for tracking update dates and responsible persons, rather than maintaining separate date fields.*

### 3.2. Metadata and Taxonomy

A managed metadata term set will be created for tagging services with standardized terms. The taxonomy will include:

  - Administrative Support
  - IT Services

- **Locations**

## 4. Functional Requirements

### 4.1. Service Directory Main Features

1. **Service Listing**
   - SharePoint list view showing all services
   - Custom grouped views by category, location, etc.
   - Summary cards with key information
   - Detailed view with all service information

2. **Search Functionality**
   - PnP search integration
   - Custom search refiners based on metadata
   - Saved search queries using SharePoint personal views
   - Keyword search across all text fields

3. **Service Management**
   - SharePoint list forms for adding/editing services
   - Version history tracking for all changes
   - Automated notifications for reviews and updates

4. **User Permissions**
   - SharePoint item-level permissions
   - Service Owners granted contributor access to their services
   - Small admin group granted edit access to all services
   - General staff given reader access

5. **Notifications**
   - Email notifications for content updates
   - Teams notifications for critical changes
   - Alert subscriptions for interested users

6. **Export Functions**
   - Export to Excel functionality

### 4.2. User Interface Requirements

1. **Main Directory View**
   - Modern SharePoint list view with custom formatting
   - Card view for visual presentation
   - Quick filters for common search parameters
   - Sorting options for various fields
   - *TBC - Mobile-responsive design for access on various devices*

2. **Service Detail View**
   - SharePoint display form with custom formatting
   - Related services and resources section

3. **Service Edit View**
   - SharePoint edit form with field validation
   - Guided input experience with help text
   - Rich text editors for formatted content
   - Image and document upload capabilities

4. **Search Interface**
   - PnP search results page with custom layout
   - Refiners panel for filtering results
   - Preview cards for search results

## 5. Key Processes

### 5.1. Create Service Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Service Owner identifies new service] --> B[Create draft entry in directory]
    B --> C[Complete required fields]
    C --> D[Internal stakeholder review]
    D --> E{Approved?}
    E -- No --> C
    E -- Yes --> F[Change status to Published]
    F --> G[Service appears in directory]
```

### 5.2. Update Service Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Need to update service identified] --> B[Service Owner sets status to Draft]
    B --> C[Update service information]
    C --> D{Significant changes?}
    D -- Yes --> E[Accountable Person review]
    D -- No --> F[Change status to Published]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Users notified of update]
```

### 5.3. Read/Search Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User needs service information] --> B[Navigate to Service Directory]
    B --> C{Search method?}
    C -- Name/Keyword --> D[Enter search term]
    C -- Browse/Filter --> E[Apply relevant filters]
    E --> F[View filtered results]
    D --> G[View search results]
    F --> H[Select service to view details]
    G --> H
    H --> I[View complete service information]
```

### 5.4. Delete/Archive Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Service discontinued or replaced] --> B[Service Owner requests deletion]
    B --> C{Service in use?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Change status to Archived]
    C -- No --> E[Admin deletes service]
    D --> F[Service remains searchable but marked as archived]
    E --> G[Service removed from directory]
```

## 6. Technical Requirements

### 5.1. Platform Components

The Service Directory will leverage the following SharePoint components:

- **SharePoint List**: Primary data storage
- **SharePoint Views**: Customized ways to display service information
- **JSON Formatted Forms**: Custom form layouts for improved data entry experience
- **PnP Search Web Parts**: Enhanced search capabilities beyond standard SharePoint search
- **SharePoint Pages**: Custom pages for directory interface
- **Modern Web Parts**: Enhanced display of directory information

### 5.2. Integration Requirements

The Service Directory will integrate with:

- **Microsoft 365**: Authentication and user profiles
- **Microsoft Teams**: Notifications and embedded views
- **SharePoint Intranet**: Surfacing service information in other contexts
- **SharePoint Analytics**: Basic usage statistics and site analytics
- **Microsoft Forms**: Potential integration for feedback collection

*Note: Power BI advanced reporting and analytics is out of scope for the initial implementation.*

### 5.3. Data Migration Strategy

1. **Source Analysis**
   - Identify existing service information sources
   - Analyze data quality and completeness
   - Map legacy fields to new data model

2. **Migration Process**
   - Extract data from existing sources
   - Transform to match new data model
   - Load into SharePoint list
   - Validate data integrity

3. **Quality Assurance**
   - Verification of migrated data
   - Service owner review and sign-off
   - Gap analysis and follow-up

### 9.1. Identified Risks

1. **Data Quality**

   - Impact: High
   - Probability: Medium
   - Mitigation: Required fields, validation, review process

2. **User Adoption**
   - Risk: Staff resistance to new system
   - Impact: High
   - Probability: Medium
   - Mitigation: Comprehensive training, clear communication of benefits

3. **Performance**
   - Risk: Slow performance with large data volume
   - Impact: Medium
   - Probability: Low
   - Mitigation: Optimized queries, indexed columns, view thresholds

4. **Permission Complexity**
   - Risk: Difficult permission management
   - Impact: Medium
   - Probability: Medium
   - Mitigation: SharePoint groups, simplified permission model

### 9.2. Contingency Plans

2. **Performance Issues**

1.1 Must Have Requirements

As a staff member, I want to search for services by various parameters, so that I can find relevant services for clients or internal needs.
As a staff member, I want to see which services are available at specific locations, so that I can refer clients to services in their area.
As a staff member, I want to know expected timeframes for support, so that I can provide accurate information to clients about service availability.
As a service leader, I want to update information about my service easily, so that all staff have access to the most current information.
As a staff member, I want to see what a service can and cannot provide, so that I can make appropriate referrals.
As a staff member, I want to see the date information was last updated and/or reviewed so that I have confidence that the information is current.
As a staff member, I want to see where the service is available so that I can inform client.
As a staff member, I want to know how to request support from an internal business service.
As a staff member, I want to know how to refer a client to the service so I can make a referral in the appropriate way.
As a staff member, I want to see alternative external services or community supports so that I can refer clients that are ineligible for the IPC Service.
As a staff member, I want to see an overview of each service so I can quickly assess if the service matches my/a client's needs.
As a staff member, I want to see any fees or costs associated with the service so that I can inform the client before I make a referral.
As a service leader, I want to know what services are using which CRM to support collaboration and client care.
As a service leader, I want to know which PROMs the service uses so that I know who to liaise with if I want to find out more about that particular PROM.
As a service leader, I want to know how a service is funded, so that I understand the context the service operates in.
As a staff member, I want to know eligibility criteria for services, so that I can determine if a client is eligible.

1.2 Should Have Requirements

As a staff member, I want to see contact information for services, so that I can direct queries appropriately.
As a staff member, I want to see what types of support are available (in-person, telehealth, etc.), so that I can inform clients of service delivery options.
As a service leader, I want to share information about group programs, so that staff can refer appropriate clients.
As a support leader, I want to share information about training my business unit offers, so that staff know what is available.
As a staff member, I want to access brochures and other resources for the service so that I can provide service information to clients.
As a service leader, I want to share key documents that inform my team's work.
As a service leader, I want to share recent research or quality improvement projects by my team so that learnings can be shared with other teams.
As a staff member, I want to know when and where teams hold regular meetings so that I can schedule collaboration, training and information sharing activities.
As a service leader, I want to provide answers to FAQ so that staff can access routine information without contacting my team.
As a staff member, I want to filter services by tags (e.g., client groups), so that I can find relevant services based on specific needs.

1.3 Could Have Requirements

As a staff member, I want to access the Service Directory on my mobile device, so that I can find information when away from my desk.
As a service leader, I want to see usage statistics for my service information, so that I can understand how often it is being accessed.
As a staff member, I want to provide feedback on service information, so that it can be continually improved.
As a staff member, I want to browse services by category, so that I can explore available services in a structured way.
As a staff member, I want to bookmark services I frequently refer to, so that I can quickly access them in the future. (TBC)

1.4 Won't Have Requirements

Public access to the Service Directory - The directory is for internal staff use only.
Integration with external referral systems - This functionality may be considered in future phases.
Automated service matching for clients - The system will provide information but not make automated service recommendations.
Team and staff profiles - These will be handled by the separate intranet project. The Service Directory is a standalone application focused only on service information.
Automated data migration - Data migration from existing sources will not be part of the initial implementation. All service information will be entered manually by Responsible Persons.
